## Intent
Hypothesis: a Halide-expressible branchless-blend loop1 parallelized via Halide, combined with a simple render loop2, can approach the streaming ceiling through auto-vectorization and parallelism.

## Cache saturation
All tested N (10K–10M) exceed the L1d spill at N≈963; N≥100K exceeds the L2 spill at N≈61680. Best-case ns/p is FLAT across N: at q=0.01, 18.058 → 17.739 → 17.584 → 17.376 for N=10K → 100K → 1M → 10M, with no knee at the L2→DRAM transition. The slight decrease is overhead amortization, not cache effects. Death rate leaves the single-thread floor flat at ~17.2–18.1 ns/p across q=0.01–0.5. No cache-spill knee confirms the algo is not streaming-bound.

## Bandwidth
Peak achieved is 3.96 GB/s at N=10000, q=0.5 — 13.2% of the 29.9 GB/s ceiling. Bandwidth is flat across N and death rate, consistent with compute-bound behavior: single-thread profiles show compute=79–88%, backend_stall=8–12%. The algo transitions to overhead-bound under multi-threading — at threads=4, backend_stall rises to 35–41% and branch_flush to 13–16%; at threads=8, backend_stall reaches 46–55% with compute collapsing to 17–27%. The streaming ceiling is never approached.

## Assembly
No vectorization: only 2 vector-suffixed instructions in 354, both `movi.2d` for zeroing. All computation is scalar — `ldp s4, s5`, `fmul s4`, `fadd s4`, `fsub s4`, `fcvtzs`, `csel` for branchless clamping. The render scatter uses byte-granular `ldrb`/`strb` (16 strb, 12 ldrb) for R/G/B read-modify-write with `cmp`/`csel` byte clamping. This scatter prevents streaming and caps bandwidth at 13% of ceiling. A `bl _halide_b2` dispatches loop1, but the render loop remains entirely scalar.

## Verdict
Refuted — the algo never exceeds 3.96 GB/s (13% of the 29.9 GB/s ceiling) because no vectorization occurred (2 `movi.2d` in 354 instructions, all scalar) and the render loop's byte-granular `ldrb`/`strb` scatter (16 strb) cannot stream. The flat ns/p (~17.5 across all N, no L2-spill knee) confirms compute-bound behavior, and multi-threading degrades performance (backend_stall 55% at 8 threads).
